_meta.indication: RELISTOR is indicated for the treatment of opioid-induced constipation in patients with advanced illness who are receiving palliative care, when response to laxative therapy has not been sufficient.

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, single-dose, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study followed by a 28-day open-label period
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with advanced medical illness (e.g. terminal illness such as incurable cancer or end-stage AIDS) and opioid-induced constipation, with a life expectancy of 1 to 6 months, who respond poorly to laxatives
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of patients with a rescue-free laxation response within 4 hours of the single double-blind treatment dose
pivotal_trials.n: 154 patients treated in the double-blind period (47 RELISTOR 0.15 mg/kg, 55 RELISTOR 0.3 mg/kg, 52 placebo)
pivotal_trials.result: Laxation within 4 hours of the double-blind dose: 62% (0.15 mg/kg) and 58% (0.3 mg/kg) vs 14% placebo; p < 0.0001 for each dose versus placebo

pivotal_trials.design: Two-week, multi-center, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel group study of MNTX given every other day (QOD)
pivotal_trials.population: Patients from U.S. and Canadian sites aged 18 to 100 with advanced medical illness and opioid-induced constipation
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary: proportion with rescue-free laxation within 4 hours after the first dose, and proportion with rescue-free laxation within 4 hours after at least two of the first four doses
pivotal_trials.result: Laxation within 4 hours of the first dose: 48% RELISTOR vs 16% placebo (p < 0.0001); laxation within 4 hours after at least 2 of the first 4 doses: 52% vs 9% placebo (p < 0.0001)

key_safety: Most common (>5%) adverse reactions: abdominal pain 28.5% (vs 9.8% placebo), flatulence 13.3% (vs 5.7%), nausea 11.5% (vs 4.9%), dizziness 7.3% (vs 2.4%), and diarrhea 5.5% (vs 2.4%).
target_moa: Methylnaltrexone bromide is a selective antagonist of opioid binding at the mu-opioid receptor; as a quaternary amine its ability to cross the blood-brain barrier is restricted, allowing it to function as a peripherally-acting mu-opioid receptor antagonist in tissues such as the gastrointestinal tract, decreasing the constipating effects of opioids without impacting central opioid-mediated analgesia.
modality: Small molecule (quaternary amine derivative of naltrexone)

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application was not referred because the product is a member of the class of previously approved opioid receptor antagonists and did not pose unique concerns.

description.text: Expanded indication to include treatment of opioid-induced constipation in adult patients with chronic non-cancer pain

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” efficacy supplemental new drug application proposes to expand the currently approved indication to include the treatment of opioid-induced constipation in adult patients with chronic non-cancer pain.

summary.text: Relistor was approved on a standard review cycle for opioid-induced constipation in patients with advanced illness receiving palliative care; it was approved first cycle as recommended by the review team, without referral to an advisory committee, with one required pediatric postmarketing (PREA) study.

citations.quote: We have completed our review of this application, as amended. It is approved, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling text.

Your application for Relistor™ was not referred to an FDA advisory committee for the following reasons. Your product is a member of the class of previously approved opioid receptor antagonists marketed in the U.S., and the product did not pose unique concerns beyond those applicable to other opioid receptor antagonists.
Your deferred pediatric study required by section 505B(a) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) is a required pediatric postmarketing study.

requirement.text: Conduct a pharmacokinetics and safety study of Relistor in pediatric patients ages 5 to 17 years with opioid induced constipation and advanced illness receiving palliative care (required pediatric assessment under PREA; final report due December 31, 2010).

citations.quote: - Conduct a pharmacokinetics and safety study of Relistor™ in pediatric patients ages 5 to 17 years with opioid induced constipation and advanced illness receiving palliative care.
